claims.wording: Disk Mop's official policy identifies Lova Software as its developer.
claims.excerpt: Disk Mop ("we", "our", "the application") is developed by Lova Software.

claims.wording: The official site advertises Disk Mop desktop v1.0.31 for macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon and Intel, with separate Mac and Intel download links.
claims.excerpt:
macOS
v1.0.31 • ~93 MB • .dmg
Apple Notarized & Signed
macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon & Intel)
claims.conditions: No installer downloaded, signature/notarization audited or compatibility tested. Earlier baseline says ~80 MB; omit installer size from drafts.

claims.wording: Disk Mop advertises disk analysis, files over 500 MB, SHA-256 duplicate detection and an interactive disk treemap.
claims.excerpt: Visually analyze disk usage. Instantly see which folders take up the most space. / Instantly detect files over 500 MB. / Find identical files using SHA-256. / Visualize your entire disk as an interactive treemap.
claims.conditions: General cross-platform page, not proof every function exists in Mac v1.0.31; no performance or safety endorsement.

claims.wording: The vendor describes a select-then-clean workflow, alongside an automatic multi-task Speed Up option.
claims.excerpt: Choose what to delete and hit the clean button. / Runs all cleanup tasks automatically.
claims.conditions: Exact per-path revalidation, confirmation dialogs, Trash versus permanent deletion, exclusions and Mac-specific controls not verified; do not imply Breathing Room-equivalent approvals.

claims.wording: The official licence FAQ describes a transferable lifetime licence for one computer without a subscription; the pricing panel includes free/lifetime updates and Windows & macOS.
claims.excerpt: 1 license = 1 computer. No subscription, no extra charges. If you change computers, you can transfer your license to the new one.
claims.conditions: No simultaneous two-device entitlement implied. Tax, refund, transfer procedure, activation limits and exact trial restrictions unknown. Dollar currency code not explicitly verified.

claims.wording: An exact current payable Disk Mop price is unresolved.
claims.excerpt: Baseline: $14.90 / $19.90 / 25% OFF one-time. Live panel: $17.91 / $19.90 / 10% OFF one-time. Live FAQ: Pay $19.90 once for lifetime access.
claims.conditions: Do not publish any as guaranteed checkout total. Preserve both observations; do not assert cause, currency code, tax inclusion or promotional expiry. No checkout/sign-in attempted.

claims.wording: Disk Mop's policy says desktop scanning, analysis and cleaning are local, with network access for licence validation and updates.
claims.excerpt: All scanning, analysis, and cleaning operations are performed locally on your device. / Your license key is verified against our licensing server (api.diskmop.com) / checks for new versions via GitHub Releases
claims.conditions: Not a network audit or proof of indefinite offline activation. Website analytics separate from desktop policy. No broad independently verified privacy guarantee.

claims.wording: Faster Boot and Service Manager descriptions explicitly reference Windows.
claims.excerpt: Measure your real startup time with Windows' own records / Control Windows services that slow down your system.
claims.conditions: Do not promise these on Mac or invent Windows support for Breathing Room.

claims.wording: Scheduled cleanup configuration is mentioned in the policy, but recurring-growth monitoring and app/helper grouping are not verified.
claims.conditions: Configuration mention does not verify schedule behavior or Mac-specific execution. Unknown helper grouping, developer-cache adapters and historical growth remain unknown, not No.

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a macOS 13+ preview; free local storage/app inspection is distinct from authenticated hosted AI and advertised AI Care at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year.
claims.excerpt: macOS 13+; universal Apple Silicon/Intel installer advertised. / $5 USD/month, $50 USD/year
claims.conditions: 0.1.0-preview.1 identified, not certified latest across channels; Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed/notarized; Python 3.10+ prerequisite; physical Intel and clean-machine testing incomplete; no Windows support established.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source implements grouped helper monitoring, activity history, developer-cache discovery and daily care with exact saved approvals while the app runs.
claims.excerpt: Native sampling groups helpers through parent/app relationships / Saved approvals bind account, API origin, action method/path and native rule
claims.conditions: Source implementation does not establish distributed-binary parity. Optional verified Ruff-cache automatic Trash mode qualifies general approval promises. Hosted requests may include paths, inventory and tool outputs. Trash moves are not immediately recovered capacity.

workflowArticle.title: Review large files and duplicates before a Mac cleanup
workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Separate a disk-map finding, a byte-identical duplicate candidate and actual deletion permission before a Mac cleanup.
workflowArticle.description: Use Disk Mop's advertised disk map and duplicate finder as discovery aids, then review ownership, backups and rebuild costs. A large file is not automatically disposable.
outline: Put a cleared real app visual directly after the lead; never restate the description
Start with a disk map and choose one folder, not a whole-disk deletion target
Treat the advertised 500 MB filter and SHA-256 matches as candidates, not deletion authority; path/reference context still matters
Separate the vendor's choose-then-clean flow from automatic Speed Up; Mac controls need confirmation
Use a keep / investigate / eligible-after-review checklist with original, duplicate and rebuildable-cache branches
Explain when one-time duplicate/treemap tooling fits and when recurring app/growth investigation calls for a different workflow
One disclosed Breathing Room recommendation with preview, Python, hosted-data and paid-care limitations
workflowArticle.distinctness: Workflow is a file-decision checklist, not an expanded feature matrix or generic alternatives list. No claims that either product was run.
workflowArticle.interactionHandoff: Implement a local-only decision checklist for file ownership, backup, references and recreation/download cost. It must never inspect/delete files or calculate invented savings; optional states only, no server calls.
internalLinks: /tools/ (only a relevant existing tool after route verification)

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Disk Mop for Mac storage decisions
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between an advertised one-time disk/duplicate toolkit and a Mac preview focused on inspectable care and activity investigation.
rows: Disk maps, large files and duplicate candidates
App/helper grouping and recurring growth (unknown is not No)
Installation caveats and exact evidence class

diskMop: Advertises a one-computer lifetime licence with updates rather than a subscription (DM05); do not use an unresolved price to claim cheaper.
Advertises duplicate detection and treemap views (DM03); their exact Mac implementation and behavior remain untested.
Vendor policy describes local scanning with licence/update network use (DM07); policy is not an independent traffic audit.
Cross-platform availability does not mean desktop/mobile feature parity or a multi-device licence. Windows service/boot descriptions must not become Mac claims.
breathingRoom: Source-backed helper grouping, activity history and developer-cache investigation suit a recurring Mac investigation intent (BR02); source is not release-runtime QA.
Free local inspection is distinct from hosted authenticated assistance and advertised paid AI Care (BR01).
Preview lacks notarization and clean-machine/physical-Intel validation; Python 3.10+ is required for inventory. Not a substitute on Windows/mobile.
Do not claim Breathing Room has a certified duplicate finder, is safer, recovers more capacity, or never deletes without a per-item prompt.
